_comment: 🧩️ This subset's own contribution to the repository test platform — the JSON RFC 8259 `any` mutation vocabulary and the reference implementation that exercises it. The FIRST draft of this manifest registered `serde_json` (already linked test-only, see `../../../../../../../../🧪️oracle/📦️packages/🦀️rust/Cargo.toml`) but that was reverted: this subset's own production code at `../🧬️schema/📸️snapshot/🦀️component.rs` declares `impl From<serde_json::Value> for JsonValue` (and the reverse), a real interop conversion path FROM the reference's own type, so a `serde_json` differential would compare this implementation against something it already converts from — not independent evidence. `json` (json-rust) 0.12 appears nowhere in this repository's production dependency graph and is used instead; see the oracle entry's `rationale` and `../🧪️oracle/🦀️component.rs`'s module doc comment for what that swap costs (member order, number precision) and how it is absorbed.

oracles.rationale: Chosen over `serde_json` specifically BECAUSE it is independent: `serde_json` is already a genuine production runtime dependency of this repository (workspace-level `serde_json = "1.0.149"`), and this subset's own production code (`../🧬️schema/📸️snapshot/🦀️component.rs`) declares `impl From<serde_json::Value> for JsonValue` / the reverse conversion — a public interop path FROM the reference's own type INTO this subset's model. A `serde_json` differential would therefore be judged by something the subject already knows how to convert from, not an independent implementation. `json` (json-rust) has no such relationship: it is a standalone recursive-descent RFC 8259 parser/serializer with its own `JsonValue`/`Object`/`Number` types unrelated to this codebase, reachable from no production file. Two real gaps versus `serde_json` (and versus this subset's own codec) are absorbed rather than hidden: `json::object::Object` stores entries in a hash-ordered binary tree keyed by an FNV-1a hash of each key (see its own source), not insertion order — RFC 8259 §4 already declares object member order insignificant, so this is covered by the SAME `ordered-json-v1` core profile (array order significant, key order never) a `serde_json` oracle would also have needed; and `json::number::Number` is a `(sign, mantissa: u64, exponent: i16)` decimal pair, not this subset's own arbitrary-precision LEXEME (RFC 8259 §6 permits arbitrary precision) — numbers are compared by parsed `f64` value, a real information-loss boundary beyond IEEE-754 double precision that the real committed fixture never crosses (verified: no number token in it exceeds 3 integer digits before any decimal point). WORKED_AROUND_DEFECT: both directions of that `Number` conversion are lossy in 0.12, and neither is a precision boundary of the format -- they move values that ARE representable as `f64`. `impl From<f64> for JsonValue` rounds INTO the decimal pair (`2.7000102824824506` dumps as `...507`, `-8.881784197001252e-16` as `...253e-16`; 2 of 9 probed values moved), and `as_f64()` rounds back OUT of it by recomputing `mantissa * 10^exponent` in floating point (the fixture's `-1.3283902924697095e-17` surface normal reads out as `...097e-17`). Both were reproduced standalone against the crate alone before being worked around, and neither is hidden: the crate's PARSER and its `dump()` are exact on every probed value, so the oracle module reaches the same `Number` through those halves -- `json::parse` of the value formatted with Rust's own shortest round-trip `{:?}` going in, `value.dump().parse::<f64>()` coming out -- and pins both the defect and the fix in its own unit tests, so a later release that fixes the conversion makes those tests fail and the workaround can go. Left unfixed, the drift is one ULP per cycle and it fails the inverse law on a defect that is not this repository's.
